When the change in target range is dominated by predator movements, a gradual upward adjustment of clicking rate is sufficient to track the changing spatial relationship of predator and prey. In comparison, unexpected rapid prey movements often provoke large adjustments in the biosonar rate in which the acoustic depth of field is rapidly expanded at the expense of temporal resolution.
